The elastic equal-mass case uses the given observation that A stops, leaving a linear unknown B velocity and an energy check; the attached opposite-velocity case requires signed total momentum and total-energy versus kinetic-energy explanation. Term evaluation plus linear equation solving supply the routines; system isolation, external impulse, collision type and internal energy remain independently visible Physics. BY Ph10.2.2 sowie BW3.3.5.3(6), HE elastischer Stoß und MV zentrale Stöße tragen diesen Kern.
